hints: Notice the wording that the glider moves at a constant speed between collisions, so the magnitude $|v|$ on the $v$-$t$ graph must stay the same.
Remember $v$ is a vector, so a perfectly elastic collision with a fixed buffer keeps the same speed but reverses the direction of motion.
Check the time for each crossing: the distance between the two fixed buffers is fixed, so equal speed means equal time between reversals.
walkthrough: Identify what is given: the air track makes friction negligible, so the glider travels with constant speed magnitude between the ends, giving horizontal lines on a $v$-$t$ graph.
State the collision rule: perfectly elastic with a massive fixed buffer means no kinetic energy loss, so speed after impact equals speed before impact, only the sign of $v$ changes.
Describe the motion in time: moving one way gives $v = +v_0$ for a time $t = L/v_0$, then instant reversal gives $v = -v_0$ for the same time $t$ on the return trip.
Combine this: the $v$-$t$ graph must be a square wave alternating between $+v_0$ and $-v_0$ with vertical jumps at impact and equal width steps.
Graphs with shrinking step height would mean energy loss and graphs with shrinking step width would mean changing travel time, neither of which applies here. This is option D

options.A: The step heights decrease, implying speed is lost at each collision, which contradicts perfectly elastic collisions at constant speed.
options.B: The step heights decrease after each reversal, implying kinetic energy is lost, which contradicts a perfectly elastic collision with a fixed buffer.
options.C: The speed magnitude is constant but the time between reversals gets shorter, which contradicts travel over the same track length at the same speed.
options.D: The graph shows constant $v$ then instant reversal to $-v$ with equal time intervals, matching constant speed and perfectly elastic reversal at each buffer.
